title: Backfill job for historical SLO calculations + migration/validation tooling
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes: Internal only. Adds a one-time + repeatable backfill workflow to compute historical SLO windows (Q4 + Q1) and validate results against raw request logs before enabling enforcement gates.
description:
Context: As part of the tiered SLO + error budget work, we need to backfill historical SLI/SLO aggregates so we can (a) validate the proposed targets against reality, (b) calibrate burn-rate alert thresholds, and (c) unblock Console work that overlays change history against budget burn. Today the budget computation job only runs forward-looking windows and assumes the aggregates table starts “now”. This PR adds a backfill workflow, a small schema migration for storage, and a validation script that compares aggregates to request logs for a sampled set of routes/models/regions.

What’s in this PR: Adds a backfill runner (argo workflow + CLI entrypoint) that can compute historical SLO windows for Hosted + Dedicated, writing results into the same aggregation tables used by the live computation job; Adds idempotent migrations for historical partitions (daily buckets) and indexes used by dashboard queries; Adds validation tooling that runs side-by-side checks for a given time range (aggregate metrics vs raw logs), with a report that highlights drift by (tier, region, route, model_family) and flags known exclusions (invalid auth, customer timeouts) so we don’t treat them as discrepancies; Adds guardrails for cardinality (enforces model_family for backfill by default; optional model label is available for narrow debugging only); Adds a dry-run mode and “resume from checkpoint” to avoid restarting long ranges.

Why now: ENG-2429 requires backfilling Q4/Q1 so we can finalize targets and make the burn-rate alerts meaningful. This also gives us confidence that the SLI spec (esp. timeouts/499s/streaming disconnect taxonomy) is being applied consistently across the metric pipeline.

Implementation details: The backfill runs in daily chunks with configurable concurrency (default 8 days in parallel) and uses the same SLI calculators as the live job; output is written with (service, tier, window, date_bucket) as the primary key to guarantee idempotency; the migration adds a “date_bucket” dimension and tightens a couple of column types for storage efficiency; validation sampling defaults to 1% of request logs with a deterministic hash on request_id to keep runs repeatable.

Operational notes: The workflow is rate-limited (token bucket) to avoid hammering the log store during business hours; recommend running with --max-qps 50 in prod; expected runtime for 2025-10-01 → 2026-01-31 is ~35–55 minutes depending on concurrency.

Rollout plan: 1) Land migration + tooling; 2) Run backfill in staging for 7 days of data; 3) Run production backfill for Q4 + Q1 (Host ed first, then Dedicated); 4) Re-run validation report; 5) Mark ENG-2429 as done and update the SLO targets doc with the resulting distributions.

Screenshots/outputs: Included in tools/backfill/README via sample validation report output.

Risks: (1) Drift between logs and metrics due to late-arriving logs or sampling; mitigated by backfill watermarking and “finalize after 48h” option. (2) Cardinality blowups if someone backfills per-model for large ranges; mitigated by defaults + explicit allowlist gating. (3) Migration locking; migration is additive and uses CONCURRENTLY where supported.

db: add date_bucket storage + indexes for historical aggregates
workflow: add argo template for Q4/Q1 backfill runs
tools: add validation script (metrics vs logs) + sample report
review_conversation: 2026-02-12 Rafael Mendes: Can we guarantee idempotency if a day is partially written and we retry? Also, please confirm we’re not backfilling per-model by default (cardinality).

2026-02-12 Aisha Bello: Yes—writes are upserts keyed on (service,tier,window,date_bucket). The runner writes day-by-day; a retry replaces the bucket. Default is model_family only; per-model requires --enable-model-dimension and a allowlist file.

2026-02-13 Nadia Rahman: Validation script should treat gateway 499 vs upstream timeout carefully; otherwise we’ll flag expected drift. Can we encode the exclusions from the SLI spec as a config file so it stays in sync?

2026-02-13 Aisha Bello: Good call. Added tools/backfill/exclusions.yaml and wired the validator to reference it. Also added a note that 499 is counted as failure for availability but excluded when auth_invalid=true.
2026-02-13 Logan Wright: Please add QPS limiting by default. We’ve had log store pressure from similar jobs.
2026-02-13 Aisha Bello: Added --max-qps default 50 and a time-windowed “sleep if over budget” limiter. README updated with recommended prod settings.
2026-02-14 Sergio Costa: Index looks good; please include a query example for dashboards so we can verify it hits the intended index.
